newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies end limit down, hogs off sharply.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies end limit down, hogs off sharply.

text.p: CME pork belly futures tumbled for limit losses of 3.000 cents a lb on delivery concerns while hog futures closed sharply lower on expectations of continued weak cash hog prices, traders said.

Pork bellies finished down the 3.000-cent limit in March and May with March at 75.575 cents. February ended down 2.825 cent after being limit down earlier. Hog futures closed 1.300 to 0.175 lower with April off 1.200 at 73.200 cents.
Pork bellies fell for limit losses on concern over deliveries against the February contract and on fund liquidation that touched off further sell stops late, traders said.

Some sources said one of the stoppers of deliveries Thursday may have been strong hands, but those deliveries were returned which sparked the long liquidation. A higher cash belly market and reduced slaughter pace this week provided only light early scale-down support, they said.

Recent weakness in cash pork prices and expectations of weak cash markets through the holiday on Monday kept hog futures pressured. Some sell stops and technical weakness added to losses, traders said.

Cash pork prices did not improve as expected this week and cutout values may continue to ease as ham prices are ready to fall, some traders said. Ham prices are near a seasonal top as retailers complete purchases for Easter, they said.

Adding to pressure were technical considerations. Many traders still expect April to fill the gap on the charts left after the last Hogs and Pigs report. April will likely trade down to 72800 to fill that gap, they said.
February, the first lean hog contract to expire, went off the board at noon CST, ending down 0.475 cent on the day to finish at 73.275 cents.

Declining cash hogs should result in a further setback in the index which is used for cash settlement of the contract. The latest CME lean hog index was off $0.51 at $73.38 per cwt and losses in cash markets Friday were expected to push the index down to near the February expiration, they said.
Futures will be closed Monday for the Presidents Day holiday and resume trading on Tuesday.
